replace_all: False
old_string:
  2. Answer-cardinality prior — the observed distribution of |truth| conditioned on
     how many acts were detected — trims a union that is longer than this kind of
     fact ever warrants, dropping the weakest-evidence excess first.

new_string:
  2. Answer-cardinality prior — the observed distribution of |truth| conditioned on
     how many acts were detected — trims a union that is longer than this kind of
     fact ever warrants, dropping the weakest-evidence excess first.

The two layers are deliberately unequal in strength. An act's charge is *grounded*:
the model read that act and named what it supports. The cardinality prior is only a
*prior*, so it never gets to contradict grounded evidence — it may cut the union
down toward the observed size, but never below the number of acts that actually
produced a charge. Likewise a size bucket is only used once at least
``MIN_BUCKET_OBS`` items have landed in it, so a single observation can never
retune the output. Without those two guards the prior over-trims the very
multi-charge facts the per-act union was built to recover.
